name: KamLAND cavity, Kamioka mine

coordinates.note: No official KamLAND page or paper fetched this session states numeric coordinates; per A17/A23 this is recorded as `kind: campus`/`confidence: approximate` off Wikipedia (rank 12) rather than as a fabricated `underground_lab`-precision point. KamLAND occupies the original Kamiokande cavity in the Kamioka mine, the same general underground complex as facility:kamioka-observatory's primary site (site:kamioka-mozumi-mine-super-kamiokande, owned by the japan-neutrino workstream).

notes: Wikipedia states an overburden of '105 m.w.e.' for KamLAND; this figure is inconsistent with the ~2700 m.w.e. established for the same Kamioka/Mozumi mine by facility:kamioka-observatory (sourced by the japan-neutrino workstream from the ICRR facility page and the Super-Kamiokande NIM paper) and is very likely a Wikipedia error or refers to a different overburden metric. It is deliberately NOT recorded here (`depth`/`depth_mwe` left null) to avoid citing an implausible figure; see coverage `missing_fields`.
This site is newly created by the reactor-solar-neutrino workstream under the EXISTING facility:kamioka-observatory (owned by japan-neutrino); that facility's own file was not edited.

summary.plain: The cavern in the Kamioka mine in Japan, originally dug for the first Kamiokande detector, that now holds the KamLAND reactor-antineutrino detector.
summary.technical: Underground cavity within the Kamioka mine (facility:kamioka-observatory), reusing the original Kamiokande excavation, housing the KamLAND liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector.
